name: Lung Abscess

possible: Klebsiella pneumoniae (necrotizing pneumonia, especially in diabetics/alcoholics)
pathogens.why: Lung abscess is most often a polymicrobial anaerobic process following aspiration, with the same oropharyngeal flora implicated in aspiration pneumonia but with a more indolent, necrotizing course requiring longer treatment.

investigations.why: CT better characterizes cavity size, wall thickness, and surrounding parenchymal involvement, and helps distinguish abscess from other cavitary lesions (e.g., malignancy, TB).

investigations.test: Sputum culture (including anaerobic culture if obtainable)
investigations.why: May identify causative organisms, though anaerobic cultures are technically difficult to obtain without invasive sampling.
May identify the organism if bacteremic spread has occurred.

reason: Prolonged fever with cough and foul-smelling sputum, particularly in a patient with aspiration risk, is consistent with lung abscess — a necrotizing pulmonary infection requiring prolonged anaerobic-active antibiotic therapy and imaging to define extent and guide drainage decisions if needed.
